message.content:
**Compounded interest**

Using the standard compound‑interest formula  
\(A = P(1 + r)^n\)

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| \(P\) | Principal ($10{,}000$) |
| \(r\) | Annual nominal interest rate (0.05 = 5%) |
| \(n\) | Number of periods (years) – here 3 |

---

### Step 1 – Compute accumulated balance  

\[
A \;=\; \$10\,000 \times (1+0.05)^3 
   \;=\; \$10\,000 \times 1.157625 
   \;\approx\$11\,576.25
\]

So after three years you would have about **$11,576.25**.

### Step 2 – Determine the interest earned  

Interest earned \(I = A - P\):

\[
I \;=\; \$11\,576.25 - \$10\,000 
    \;\approx\$1\,576.25
\]

---

#### Result

After 3 years at an annual rate of 5 % (with yearly compounding), your investment grows from **$10,000** to approximately **$11,576.25**, yielding a total compounded interest gain of roughly **$1,576.25**.
